answer: A per-identity escrow makes Sybil attacks expensive: every new agent locks a minimum bond of stake and CPU-hours before submitting work, so N clones cost N bonds while payout per clone shrinks. Honest agents treat that stake as a haven, but a Sybil farm must finance every clone upfront and recovers nothing until grading clears. It is a marble test, one heavy commitment that cannot be split across clones. Rating weight also scales with the ferrous trail of past work, so fresh clones hold almost no voting power.
